records.category: procurement irregularities found by the state audit institution
records.people: Leonardo Ovidio Reyes Ramirez (President, BCN); Sara Amelia Rosales Castellon (General Manager); Melba Elena Mendoza Cabrera and Carlos German Sequeira Lacayo (Managers, Institutional Management Division); Arlen Lissette Perez Vargas (Procurement Manager); Luis Angel Montenegro E., Marisol Castillo Bellido and Maria Dolores Aleman Cardenal (Consejo Superior, CGR)
records.summary: In resolution RIA-UAI-649-2024 of 29 February 2024 the Consejo Superior of Nicaragua's Contraloria General de la Republica ruled on a compliance audit of the Banco Central de Nicaragua's procurement covering 1 January 2019 to 31 December 2020 (report IN-014-002-23 of 27 November 2023). Of four findings it confirmed two and dismissed two, made the recommendations attached to the two confirmed findings binding on the bank's highest authority within 60 calendar days, and found no grounds to establish responsibility against the named BCN officials, including President Leonardo Ovidio Reyes Ramirez.
records.detail: The two dismissed findings concerned acts in procurement processes 13-35-20 and 21-86-19 and public tender 05-12-20 said to have been carried out by unauthorised personnel, and alleged failures in the procedures for contract modification, renewal, payment, return of guarantees and substitution of evaluation-committee and contract-administration members; the Consejo held both unsupported. Findings 2 and 4 were confirmed but their content is not described in the resolution, so the conduct behind them is not stated here. The subject of the audit is the central bank itself, not a ministry. Every date, reference number and person above is taken from the resolution at the source URL. No verbatim quote is filed because the document was read through a fetch summary rather than copy-pasted, and brief_common.md requires a pasted quote or none.
records.source_title: Resolucion RIA-UAI-649-2024, Consejo Superior, Contraloria General de la Republica de Nicaragua, on Informe de Auditoria de Cumplimiento IN-014-002-23 of the Banco Central de Nicaragua

records.category: undocumented state transfers executed by the central bank on ministerial instruction
records.people: Marie Carmele JEAN MARIE (Minister of Finance); Ronald Grey DECEMBRE (Secretary of State / Minister of Finance); Charles CASTEL (Governor, BRH); Maryse NOEL (Director General, Ministry of Tourism)
records.summary: Haiti's Cour Superieure des Comptes et du Contentieux Administratif, in the second PetroCaribe report of 31 May 2019, traced two disbursements for the Hotel La Jacmelienne rehabilitation made through the Banque de la Republique d'Haiti on written instructions from finance ministers to Governor Charles CASTEL, and found no supporting documents for either: 30,000,000 HTG credited to Ministry of Tourism public-investment account 121 252 331 on 5 April 2013 after a 3 April 2013 letter from Minister Marie Carmele JEAN MARIE, and USD 1,700,000 on 22 July 2014 on the instructions of Ronald Grey DECEMBRE.
records.detail: The Court records (paragraphs 468-471 of rapport 2) that the project cost USD 5,500,000, that USD 2,396,320.64 was disbursed, that the second payment was a director's cheque payable to notary Clermont DOSSOUS for acquisition of the building that had housed the hotel, that no document evidencing the acquisition was traced, and that its own technical team found the site abandoned and dilapidated. The subject of the finding is the Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Tourism; the BRH is the counterparty that executed the transfers on instruction and is not itself accused, so this is filed with counterparty_only true and does not colour the row. All names, amounts, account numbers and dates above appear in the report at the source URL. Distinct from the record the map holds for Haiti (Venel Joseph, 2004) and from the 2011 parliamentary summons on the removals row.
records.source_title: Cour Superieure des Comptes et du Contentieux Administratif, Rapport d'audit specifique de gestion des fonds PetroCaribe, deuxieme rapport, 31 mai 2019

records.central_bank: Centrale Bank van Curacao en Sint Maarten
records.category: unlawful state borrowing routed through the central bank
records.people: Minister of Finance of Curacao (not named on the page); Algemene Rekenkamer Curacao
records.summary: Auditing the Government of Curacao's 2023 annual accounts, the Algemene Rekenkamer Curacao found two loans totalling more than 700 million guilders on the state balance sheet with no valid legal basis and classified both as unlawful obligations. One of them, 291 million guilders for GI-RO Settlement Holding, was issued in 2020 through the Centrale Bank van Curacao en Sint Maarten without the authorisation the Minister of Finance is required to give by formal government decree. This rests on the Curacao Chronicle's report of the Algemene Rekenkamer's findings rather than on the Rekenkamer's own report, which was not opened.
records.detail: The other loan was nearly 433 million guilders recorded as financing for Hospital Nobo Otrobanda Vastgoed en Beheer N.V., provided in 2020 with no loan agreement ever concluded, and the CBCS is not named in the findings on it. The Audit Chamber says both loans stayed on the books for years without corrective action, which it links to systemic shortcomings in financial control and legal compliance, and concludes the 2023 accounts do not give a reliable picture of Curacao's financial position. The subject of the finding is the government and the Minister of Finance; the CBCS is only the channel through which the loan was issued and is not accused of wrongdoing, so counterparty_only is true and this does not colour the row. The record rests on the Curacao Chronicle's report of 30 December 2025 on the Rekenkamer's audit rather than on the Rekenkamer's own report, which this round did not open. Distinct from the Emsley Tromp and Rene Laurents convictions the map already holds for Curacao.
records.source_title: Audit chamber flags deep governance risks after 700 million in unlawful state loans, Curacao Chronicle, 30 December 2025

blanks.note: Inversion test passed and answered in the negative. Audit Office of Guyana, Auditor General's Report on the Public Accounts for 2022 (9.9 MB, downloaded and grepped in full, 1.49 million characters of extracted text), section 'Audit of Statutory Bodies', table 'Unqualified Opinions - In-house': the Bank of Guyana appears as entity number 3 and the Bank of Guyana Pension Scheme as number 4, year of audit 2022, both under UNQUALIFIED opinions. So the Auditor General does audit the central bank and issued a clean opinion for 2022. Every other mention of 'Bank of Guyana' in the report (31 hits, all read) is the bank as account holder, debenture issuer, exchange-rate source or supervisor: the PDVSA escrow account opened at the bank's request on 17 January 2018 and properly recorded, Treasury bill and debenture issues, Deposit Insurance Fund contributions, and one disclaimed opinion on a Department whose ledger differed from its Bank of Guyana reconciliation by 75.600M, where the subject is the Department. Nothing against the bank. Checked against index 239 (1.8 billion in eight unused BoG accounts, 2015): the dormant-accounts finding does not recur in the 2022 report at all.

Inversion test run on the Algemene Rekenkamer Aruba's own mapping of the public sector. 'Publieke sector in beeld' (Algemene Rekenkamer Aruba, 2.4 MB, downloaded and grepped in full): the Centrale Bank van Aruba (CBA) is listed as entity 3 under 'Ministerie van Financien, Communicatie, Utiliteiten en Energie' in the overview of publiekrechtelijke rechtspersonen, with its legal basis the Centrale Bankverordening (AB 1991 No. GT 32). The row records only the accountability mechanism - annual reporting in May, a jaarverslag and a financieel verslag, not part of the Land's jaarrekening, controlled by the CAD or an external accountant - and states no finding, irregularity or amount against the bank. The CBA is mentioned nowhere else in the document. Separately, the Rekenkamer's report on the Land's 2011 annual accounts (6.9 MB) was downloaded and grepped: the word 'bank' does not occur in its 92,700 characters of extracted text, so it carries nothing on the CBA either. Vein for Aruba: the Rekenkamer knows the CBA exists as an audited public body but has published no finding against it in the two documents read.

blanks.type: vein closed on two documents, open on the series
blanks.note: Two further CGR resolutions in the same BCN series were read and are clean, and are recorded here so the next round does not spend fetches on them. RIA-UAI-364-16 (Consejo Superior resolution of 11 March 2016, on BCN internal audit report IN-014-009-2015 of 28 August 2015, on the Fondo de Ahorro Complementario de los Empleados del BCN for the year to 31 December 2014): financial statements fairly presented, 'No se revelo condiciones reportables de control interno', compliance in all material respects, no hallazgos, no officials named. RIA-UAI-1025-18 (resolution of 12 October 2018, session 1,108, on report IN-014-005-2018 of 18 September 2018, same FAC fund, years to 31 December 2016 and 2017): fairly presented, internal control complied with in all significant respects, all three recommendations from report IN-014-007-2012 of 16 April 2012 implemented, no hallazgos. Note for the next round: the CGR repository at cgr.gob.ni holds roughly twenty 'ria uai ... bcn' resolutions from 2013 to 2024 under /index.php/repositorio/send/<folder>/<id>-ria-uai-..., so the series is the richest untested seam in this assignment. The 'aees' and 'acum' codes carry special and compliance audits of the bank itself; the 'afyc' codes read so far are financial audits of the staff savings fund and come back clean. curl is reset by the host on these paths; WebFetch serves them.

blanks.type: vein closed on one document, open on the series
blanks.note: The CSCCA's first PetroCaribe report of 31 January 2019 (7.2 MB, downloaded and grepped in full) was read for the BRH and carries no finding against the bank: all 14 hits are the bank as domicile of the PetroCaribe and CSTD accounts, as the source of the discount rate used for moratorium interest in construction contracts, or the Governor sitting as one of seven members of the BMPAD board alongside six ministers. The second report of 31 May 2019 is the one that converted, on the Hotel La Jacmelienne transfers. Also noted in the second report and NOT filed, because the bank is the detector rather than the subject: at paragraph 674 the Court records that information furnished by the BRH allowed it to establish that a start-up advance on an MPCE stadium contract had been disbursed from PetroCaribe funds outside the resolutions. One document on this host 404s: the '15 ans de finances publiques' report at m.cscca.gouv.ht/uploads/bannieres/documents/1765466699_cscca_rapport_15_ans_finances_publiques.pdf returned a 6,603-byte HTML 'Not Found' page to curl and was not retried. The CSCCA's budget-execution reports for 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25 and the RSFPEDP series are on the same host and untested.

A PwC investigation report on the Centrale Bank van Curacao en Sint Maarten exists and was downloaded (Rapport-PWC-Centrale-Bank-CBCS-Samenvatting, 142,531 bytes, hosted by knipselkrant-curacao.com under a 2015 upload path). It is a scan: pdftotext extracts zero characters. It was not OCRed for want of budget. It is the strongest untested CUW document and would cost one OCR pass, no fetch, since the file is a known-good URL from a search result. It may or may not overlap the Emsley Tromp episode the map already holds. The Algemene Rekenkamer Curacao's own report on the Government's 2023 annual accounts was also not opened; only the Curacao Chronicle's report of it was.

The Camara de Cuentas' own publications index was again not opened, so round 71's note stands: a search of its output returns only press coverage of the reports it has approved (Promipyme, Banca Solidaria, Senasa, Policia Nacional, MIVED, Camara de Diputados, Hacienda, INAIPI, MICM, SIPEN, EdeEste, IDAC, municipalities, Ministerio de Salud Publica) and nothing naming the Banco Central as an audited entity. Two searches this round returned no camaradecuentas.gob.do URL at all, which is why the inversion test still has not been run; the next round should reach the index through a search that returns the host itself rather than news coverage. The record filed above came from the Camara de Cuentas' report on the central government's financial statements, where the bank is the counterparty, not the audited entity.

One search spent, no fetch. It returned the same AuGD work round 71 found - Development Bank of Jamaica, Tax Administration Jamaica, the Accountant General's Department, the MLSS, the Courts, the jampja.org breach database - plus the AuGD annual reports for 2016-17 and 2020 and the Bank of Jamaica's own 2024 and 2025 annual reports, and nothing on the Bank of Jamaica as an audited entity. Round 71's note that the bank's accounts are audited by private external auditors rather than by the Auditor General is consistent with this. Untested and named for the next round: the Bank of Jamaica annual reports at boj.org.jm/2024-boj-annual-report-final and /2025-boj-annual-report-final, to be grepped for an integrity or disciplinary disclosure, and the parliamentary route at japarliament.gov.jm, which is where the removals-row record for Jamaica came from.

One search spent, no fetch. No Office of the Auditor General report naming the Central Bank of The Bahamas was returned; what came back was AuGD work on the Ministry of Tourism's health visa contracts, Mayaguana local government, the Bahama Games, and a 'gross manipulation of public monies' finding, none of them about the central bank, plus the bank's own annual reports for 2014 and 2018-2022 and its Internal Audit Guidelines of 2022. Named for the next round and untested: the bank's 'Final Internal Audit Guidelines 2022' and the annual reports and statements of accounts on centralbankbahamas.com, to be grepped for a governance or internal-discipline disclosure, and the Public Accounts Committee of the House of Assembly, which was not reached again this round.

No search or fetch was spent on Cuba. Budget went to the four countries that converted plus the Guyana and Aruba inversion tests. Round 71's note stands untested: the Contraloria General de la Republica de Cuba is not established to publish per-entity audit reports, and whether it publishes anything naming the Banco Central de Cuba has still not been checked. The country has not been tested.

No search or fetch was spent on Venezuela. Round 71's note stands untested: the Contraloria General de la Republica de Venezuela's per-entity reports are the nominal route and are unlikely to be published for the BCV, but that has not been checked here and should not be assumed. The country has not been tested.

checked_not_in_assignment.note: No country outside the ten assigned was researched or filed. One candidate surfaced incidentally and was deliberately not pursued: Sint Maarten, because the Curacao finding above concerns a loan issued through the Centrale Bank van Curacao en Sint Maarten, which serves both. The finding is about the Government of Curacao's own 2023 annual accounts and the Curacao Minister of Finance, so it is keyed to CUW alone and not expanded to SXM. SXM is not in this assignment and was not looked up further.
